Physiological dead space is the space within the lungs that is ventilated but not perfused. This is usually the space within the respiratory dead space (consonant space) which is the area which is ventilated but not perfused with blood. This can be increased in diseased states such as the paralysis of the respiratory muscles. This is because the muscles of respiration are paralysed and so the lungs do not inflate fully and there is an increase in the area of the lungs which is not perfused with blood. This is called hypoventilation because the ventilation:perfusion ratio is decreased. This is because the ventilation:perfusion ratio is normally 0.8 and this is the ideal ratio for gas exchange to occur. If the ratio is higher than this then this means that there is too much dead space and not enough perfusion to allow for gas exchange to occur.
